paper.title: Safe havens or war hedges? Asset behavior during the 2026 escalation of the Iran conflict
paper.paper_claim: Gold and Bitcoin were not robust safe havens around the 2026 Iran escalation, while oil displayed the clearest short-run war-hedge behavior.

hypothesis: Around the 2026-02-27 Iran escalation shock, oil-linked exposure protects an equity portfolio more effectively than gold or Bitcoin over the short event window.

decision_gate.condition_if: For the 2026-02-20 through 2026-03-06 event window, an 80% SPY / 20% hedge portfolio improves cumulative return, maximum drawdown, and daily 95% Expected Shortfall versus SPY alone, while gold and Bitcoin do not both satisfy the same three-metric gate.
decision_gate.reject_if: Oil-linked exposure fails the same three-metric gate or is not better than the gold and Bitcoin alternatives.

canonical_real_data.equity_and_etf_source: Alpaca Market Data Stock Bars, IEX feed
canonical_real_data.crypto_source: Alpaca Market Data Crypto Bars, US feed
canonical_real_data.timezone: America/New_York for equity bars; BTC/USD aligned exactly to the listed US-equity trading dates
canonical_real_data.identity_note: This is an independent tradable-proxy replication, not an exact reproduction of the paper's Refinitiv MSCI World, spot/commodity, and volatility-regression dataset.

method.benchmark: SPY buy-and-hold over the fixed event window
method.portfolio_return_convention: Daily constant-weight diagnostic return: 0.8 * SPY daily return + 0.2 * hedge daily return.
method.expected_shortfall: Mean of worst 5% daily returns; with 10 returns this equals the single worst daily return and is therefore only an event-window diagnostic.
method.transaction_cost_note: No repeated trading strategy is claimed. The test evaluates a pre-positioned 20% hedge sleeve during one event, so no turnover optimization or after-cost alpha claim is made.

benchmark_comparison.key_observation: Only the 20% USO sleeve improved cumulative return, maximum drawdown, and daily 95% Expected Shortfall simultaneously versus SPY during the fixed event window.

claim_boundary: CONDITION applies only to the event-specific principle that oil-linked exposure behaved as the stronger short-run war hedge than gold or Bitcoin during the 2026 Iran escalation in this independent tradable-proxy replication. It does not establish oil as a general safe haven, a permanent portfolio sleeve, or a profitable ex-ante geopolitical trading strategy.
portfolio_implication: Do not assume gold or Bitcoin automatically hedge geopolitical equity shocks. For supply-disruption conflicts, oil-linked exposure can be evaluated explicitly as a short-run hedge candidate, but any reusable allocation rule requires multi-event out-of-sample validation and implementable entry timing/costs.
do_not_use_for: claims that oil is a universal safe haven
claims that Bitcoin or gold never hedge geopolitical shocks
